requiredScope: All previously required families, releases and modes remain in scope.

Select.role: Root of a projection over two ordinary external inputs in a RIGHT join
Select.structure: Closed left and right occurrences, their ordered predicate and explicit ordered result fields
Select.conditions: Both headings are complete and contain unique names. Native analyzed syntax uses one join, with declared keys and no conflicting NATURAL clause. The existing constructor validates reference scope.
Select.meaning: Evaluate ON equality pairs in written input order, and NULL-extend the left occurrence for unmatched right rows. Output labels and expressions encode visibility and merged provenance.
Select.sql: Emit RIGHT JOIN with its explicit predicate and result list. Unconstrained RIGHT is allowed when NATURAL has no common names.

ResultColumn.role: A visible output position and its resolved value in a RIGHT merge
ResultColumn.structure: Exact result label and a complete scalar expression
ResultColumn.conditions: The binder determines labels before publishing. The result owner checks the scalar against actual input slots.
ResultColumn.meaning: An unqualified star keeps the left heading position and spelling for a merged key but reads the right value. An explicit unqualified column use reads the right slot and takes its declared spelling absent an alias. A qualified use retains the original occurrence and spelling. Under the pinned release, a left qualified star also reads the right representative in each merged position and retains every item of its own heading.
ResultColumn.sql: Render the bound expression and its explicit label. Independent owners may reuse the right slot under distinct result labels.

ColumnReference.role: The exact original or right representative slot
ColumnReference.conditions: The analyzer resolves each role to one exact physical slot. SELECT checks scope before construction succeeds.
ColumnReference.meaning: Read the affinity, collation and value of the referred slot. For an unqualified merged reference, this is the right slot even on a matched pair. Qualified names distinguish both input cells.
ColumnReference.sql: Use the original occurrence's generated qualifier and declared column name.

externalInterpretation: SQLite evaluates the same absolute relations, declared column affinities and collations, and rows. The resolved IR stores no declarations or analysis context.
observations: A matched NOCASE pair can hold different values. The RIGHT representative remains the exact right BINARY string and its declared name where native name rules select it.
A matched TEXT and NUMERIC pair can hold different storage classes. The merged output follows the right class. A predicate consuming a merged column inherits the right affinity and collation.
Unmatched right rows, NULL keys, duplicate matches, exact output names and positions, and both separately qualified inputs.
When NATURAL has no common columns, the unqualified star retains the full ordered headings and no equality is emitted.
The qualified left star and a list of explicitly qualified column names differ on a matched pair and on a right-only row. Compare both forms.

finite.completeness: Visit all 24 combinations exactly once. Independently identify them from the emitted public graph.

exploration.structure: Generate different orientation, key counts and repetitions, right and left reference roles, projection width, ordering of fields and generated labels.

analysis: Admit the exact former RIGHT USING rejection.
NATURAL RIGHT star retains left heading order and spelling while reading the right merged cells.
Qualified stars keep both complete ordered headings. A left qualified star still reads the right representative in a merged position on SQLite 3.47.2.
Case-varied unqualified uses, parenthesized name, and qualified names each take native spelling.
Reversed input orientation changes column comparison and representative value.
A disjoint NATURAL RIGHT join has no ON and no suppressed field.
A merged WHERE name uses the right BINARY collation.
A merged WHERE name uses the right numeric affinity.
negative: The compared right column slot is missing.
A merged RIGHT over a prefix of joins has no admitted binary derivation.
A FULL merge has a different representative rule and remains an explicit refusal.
The name of a USING key is absent from a complete heading.
faults: Read the left occurrence in a projected right representative.
Emit LEFT instead of RIGHT, losing right-only rows.
Drop the final output field, losing a qualified value.
Remove the second equality in a two-key RIGHT join.

evidence.P01: Measure named operand and result references directly in the published graph.
evidence.P02: Observe typed rejection at construction or at analysis before publication.
evidence.P03: The normalized RIGHT join uses the same closed values as direct construction.
evidence.P04: Derive right-row groups, NULL extension and each projected field from explicit operands.
evidence.P05: Replay the immutable closed role graph and installed composition.
evidence.P06: Compare actual SQL and native source syntax to an independent right-pair model.
evidence.Q01: Verify normalized references and checked positive and negative boundaries.
evidence.Q02: Require every finite identity, analyzed input and seeded case.
evidence.Q03: Check both directions of value selection independently from the source parser.
evidence.Q04: Require the real engine to agree with typed effects and rows in each checked case.
evidence.Q05: Tie the observed PHP sources, renderer mutants and native results to the fixed manifest.

open: FULL selects the first non-NULL of both merged slots and has separate unaliased name and affinity rules.
Merged joins involving multiple prefix inputs, local definitions, views or virtual tables remain open.
trust: Native SQLite 3.47.2 join, short-column-name and comparison rules
Fixed analysis boundaries and verified distribution
